what_happened: Task 379 (the declared dependency) was found already implemented/landed in this repo's validate-state.sh (--archive mode, Checks A1-A6 live) during research verification, so the dependency edge imposes no actual wait at plan time; the archive-sibling-reading idiom (Check D3's $state_dir/archive/state.json union pattern) was also confirmed reusable verbatim for the new staleness check rather than needing a new archive reader.

Research report's claim that state-write.sh has no dedicated test suite was wrong in a useful direction: scripts/test-state-write-concurrency.sh (flat, not under tests/, 536 lines, 9 cases) already owns state-write.sh with an isolated temp root and a fixtured sibling archive. Landing --allocate-into coverage there avoided a new test file and therefore avoided editing agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json, which is claimed by four not_started records (282, 313, 435, 436) and would have required dependency edges.

Every file in the dispatch's conditional per-caller scope list carries at least two non-terminal claimants (commands/task.md: 328 planned plus 384/407/435/438 not_started; the three SKILL.md callers: 328/384/435), on top of the 391 and 313 conflicts the dispatch already named. Per-caller migration was therefore excluded from the plan rather than adding dependency edges serializing this record behind not_started work; the primitive lands opt-in and documented, and the exclusion plus required edges are recorded in the plan's Decisions section.

Landing Check 12 in validate-state.sh (Phase 1) makes the pre-existing D6b fixture (d6-archived-fixture.json, next_project_number=999201, active max 999200) newly FAIL: the suite's shared sibling archive/state.json used by Check D6 fixtures carries completed_projects project_number 999210, which is higher than this fixture's own counter and active max. This is an incidental cross-fixture numbering collision in test-validate-state.sh unrelated to what the D6b fixture tests (archived-parent lineage, not counter staleness) -- exactly the case the plan's risk table names ('Existing test-validate-state.sh fixtures newly fail Check 12', mitigated by 'Phase 3 re-runs the whole suite to confirm against the fixtures that measurement could not parse'). Deferring the one-line fixture-number fix to Phase 3, which already owns test-validate-state.sh edits and explicitly re-confirms pre-existing cases.

Phase 6's base-mode consumer audit confirmed no existing caller of validate-state.sh newly blocks on the new Check 12 FAIL: of the dispatch-enumerated callers, only verify-deploy.sh gate 10 and test-init-specs.sh actually inspect the exit status, and both pass against the live tree and the fresh-init template respectively; every other named caller either only mentions validate-state.sh in a comment or structurally discards/filters the exit status before use (commands/task.md Step 6.5's grep pipe; update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add's scratch-copy line-grep). The full gate set (bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh's self-verify) landed RESULT=landed_verify_clean with 37/37 checks passing on the first load-eased retry, after two earlier attempts timed out under heavy concurrent sibling load (confirmed pre-existing load-sensitive gate10 flakiness per known-failures.txt row 33, not a Check 12 regression -- a direct standalone validate-state.sh --deep timing came in at 10.7s, far under the 30s budget).
